title: Optimize Toolchains for Maximum Compile Speed
description: No dev or agent uses a step-through debugger anymore; debugging is console-log only. Reconfigure Rust (Cargo profiles, release incremental, codegen-units), TypeScript (incremental type-check), VS Code extension Vite builds (drop sourcemaps), Python (drop debugpy), .vscode/launch.json (zero debug adapters), and C# (no PDBs) for maximum compile/build speed, given a 193-crate Rust workspace where the hot path is wasm-pack/wasip2/native --release builds.
summary:
Reconfigured every toolchain for maximum compile/build speed now that no dev or agent uses a step-through debugger (console-log-only debugging).

Rust: root Cargo.toml [profile.dev] drops debuginfo (debug=false, removed split-debuginfo) and [profile.release] gains incremental=true + codegen-units=256 (user-approved compile-speed-over-runtime tradeoff) + lto="off", keeping strip="debuginfo" (strip="symbols" breaks wasm per rust-lang/rust#93294). Verified: a wasm-pack --release build of imperative/core dropped from 23s cold to 0.82s cargo / 2.3s total on a leaf-crate touch (release-incremental works); cargo build -p compose-store --release succeeded (native release path); cargo test -p vcs --lib passed 38/38 under the new dev profile (debug=false doesn't break test binaries).

TypeScript: flipped incremental:false→true + added tsBuildInfoFile in tsconfig.json, ui/js/react, compose/dev/algorithm/js, compose/client/lib/js.

VS Code extension builds: sourcemap:true→false in repo/client/vscode/js/vite.config.ts and all three sourcemap flags in compose/client/ui/vscode/js/vite.config.ts (kept minify:false). Verified directly via vite (bypassing a pre-existing unrelated nx cwd bug in both build scripts) — no .map files emitted.

Python: removed debugpy>=1.8.21 from root pyproject.toml dev deps, regenerated uv.lock (debugpy remains only as ipykernel's transitive dep, which is correct). Removed devcontainer.json's forwarded port 5678 "Python Debugger".

launch.json: converted the one "type": "node" config (🛠️dev🔬coda🤖mcp) to "node-terminal" — all 213 configs are now debug-adapter-free.

C#: added <DebugType>none</DebugType> + <DebugSymbols>false</DebugSymbols> to all 9 tracked csproj files. Verified via dotnet build -c Release on Elements.Styling.csproj — no .pdb emitted.

Explicitly rejected (researched, documented in plan): Cranelift codegen backend (no wasm32 support, panic=abort breaks cargo test, arm64-macOS ABI issues), strip="symbols" globally, opt-level drop, panic="abort", Nx daemon re-enable (user chose to keep disabled).

Found and flagged as separate out-of-scope tasks (not fixed here): (1) both VS Code extension build pipelines (repo/client/vscode and compose/client/ui/vscode) are pre-existing broken due to a prior commit moving vite.config.ts into a js/ subfolder without updating the invoking script's cwd or output paths; (2) coda/client/bin/assistant/py/main.py imports google.genai but it's missing from pyproject.toml dependencies, so the coda assistant MCP server crashes on startup; (3) .vscode/launch.json's coda mcp config's --directory arg (coda/assistant) doesn't match the real path (coda/client/bin/assistant/py) — pre-existing, unrelated to the node→node-terminal conversion made here.
